Venison. The best meat in the woods, and the saddest. Thank it. It's dead. The carcass is there on the ground — search the body if you want the meat. But you don't know this flesh. Clean it, test it cautiously, or ask someone who knows. And don't leave it long: meat rots where it lies.

🕯️ Anh Krawczyk is dead — a stranger. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
What Anh kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
The village's quarrel was with Anh — and Anh is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
At the grave, Jae speaks for Ming — "Anh trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
That night, they bring Anh home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.

fightLines.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Anh Krawczyk. Dockworker. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Wedding ring, Photo album, Notebook, Dispatcher's headset, Seed packet. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. They found a deer this morning. Inside out. Not eaten — unmade. Like something was trying to understand how it worked. It didn't finish.
You remember the Stone knife at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
You remember the Work Gloves at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
Hunger gnaws. The pack is thin — work the green, haul it back, get it named at camp. That's the whole game.

🔥 The fire settles. Brian has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Hushpuppy — I put it down today." "No telegraph you can hear. Watch the birds — when they go quiet, the pack is already moving." "The pack circles — nips from the edge, never committing." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Anthony asks "So it bleeds." Farid breathes "Did it look at you? Before?" Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

◈ RESONANCE HARMONICS — SYSTEM: "HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED. Objects with high observer-attention waveforms function as auxiliary capacitors. We call this RESONANCE HARMONICS. We do not know why the waveforms taste like grief. We have stopped asking." — Hold a keepsake. Think about them. The System will do the math. (It is not math. It is love. The System will never know.)
